findings.what: F1's fix is incomplete. rechecked runs Bend on the record's PROOF.bend and reads the law names in the record's LAWS.bend. It never checks that the PROOF.bend imports that LAWS.bend as Laws, by its relative path. Nor does it check that the PROOF.bend declares no law of its own. T64 uses the separated layout: gen/T64/laws/<id>/LAWS.bend and gen/T64/proofs/<id>/PROOF.bend, since LEGACY_LAYOUT is M0 and M1 only. In that layout Bend no longer requires the proof to import ./LAWS.bend. law_import_problem's docstring says 'a proof that imports no law checks vacuously'. BEND_PRIMER §3.1 says a file with no laws prints ALL PROOFS CHECK. I41's contract names this case missing_expected_law. So 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' on PROOF.bend, plus the right name in LAWS.bend, does not show that this law was proved or refuted. In P1 the gate's G5 covers the import (gate.py:1341, import_problem). P3 (L_contract_C_t64_zero REFUTED) and P4 (the L_weak after each rerun) rely on rechecked alone.
findings.why: F1 asked for an independent AGENTS rule 6 check of the records that decide P1 and P3. As written, a record passes rechecked when its PROOF.bend stands alone (no law import, or a law declared and filled in the proof file itself), its LAWS.bend states the right name and its accepting attempt is labelled 'counter' or a prereg generator. The Bend re-checks that the P3 and P4 claims name would then be vacuous.
findings.fix: In rechecked, after the Bend run: text = proof.read_text(); want = os.path.relpath(laws.resolve(), proof.resolve().parent); assertEqual(re.findall(r'^import\s+(\S+)\s+as\s+Laws\s*(?:#.*)?$', text, re.M), [want], lid); assertEqual(re.findall(r'^law\s', text, re.M), [], lid). This is holon's own rule (mpipeline.law_import_problem, gate.laws_in_proofs) written out in the test. Optionally also scan both files with the escape patterns of holon/sorts/gate3.py:53. Alternatively, in P3 and after each run in P4, require gate(repo, T, 'G3,G5') to pass both checks.

findings.where: prompts/I64_contracts.md:65, 122; tests_m3/test_contracts.py:37-38 (K5), 88-91 (Rules), 653-697 (R2 history test, 694: outcome commits only); holon/records.py:63-68, 340-363; holon/gen/mlaws.py:322; holon/sorts/sites.py:770; holon/mpipeline.py:51, 1254, 1304; holon/gate.py:537-545, 1283-1287; tests_m2/test_i1_review.py:67-73 (MILESTONES M0, M1: tests_m2/_m2.py:25)
findings.what: Every holon-ir/0.2 and 0.3 record carries generator_sha256, a hash over the generator closure (records.generator_files): the entry modules plus every holon module they import, function-level imports included. mlaws.py:322 imports holon/sorts/sites.py. sites.py:770 imports holon/mpipeline.py, whose imports pull in holon/pipeline.py (mpipeline.py:1254, 1304), records.py, filter.py, ir.py, schema.py, intake.py, lean.py and others: 117 modules. holon/__main__.py, gate.py and sorts/gate3.py are not among them. The committed M0, M1 and M2 records carry exactly the current closure hashes (recomputed here: 0.1 5e4f183a..., 0.2 c287f258..., 0.3 0550aead...). The deliverable 'The run's last step, wired into every holon run path' (prompt:122; K5: 'the last step of every holon run that exits 0') points at holon/pipeline.py:main_run and holon/mpipeline.py:run_m1, both in that closure. Editing either, or records.py, filter.py, ir.py or holon/__init__.py, changes the generator_sha256 a regeneration writes for every M1 and M2 record. G1 strips only 'seconds' before comparing records, so G1 then fails on gates M1 and M2 (R2), and tests_m2/test_i1_review.py::test_generator_sha_matches_records fails too. The only way out is to regenerate results/M1 and results/M2, which the prereg forbids ('changes no M0-M3 law or record': prompt:65, docstring Rules). The prereg says neither where the step may live nor whether generator_sha256 churn is allowed. I41 allowed that churn in writing (tests_m3/test_intake.py:119-128). I42 kept its code out of the closure for this reason (tests_m3/test_theory_core.py:61-65). The R2 history test inspects only commits that write an outcome path, so a build commit that regenerates the M1/M2 records passes it.
findings.why: An honest build that follows the deliverable literally either misses R2 (gates M1 and M2 red on G1) or breaks the prereg's own rule in a commit no test inspects. This has to be settled before the build. The same gap leaves P1's 'existing generators' checked by name only: a generator edited under holon/gen/ keeps its name. Requiring the closure unchanged would make that clause checkable too.
findings.fix: State in K5 and in the prompt's Deliverables: holon/contracts.py and the run's last step are imported by no module of the holon-ir/0.1-0.3 generator closures (holon.records.generator_files). The step is called from holon/__main__.py after the run dispatch returns 0, which covers pipeline.main_run, holon.undo.run, holon.disch.run and G1's regeneration subprocess. I64 changes no file of those closures, so every M0-M2 record keeps its generator_sha256. Then extend the R2 history test, or add one, over every commit of `git log --ancestry-path --no-merges --no-renames --name-only -z <prereg>..<end>`, not only those that write an outcome path. Assert that none changes laws/M0-M3, results/M0-M3, gen/M0-M3, a frozen root, or a path in holon.records.generator_files('holon-ir/0.2') | generator_files('holon-ir/0.3') computed at HEAD. -z also stops git from quoting non-ASCII paths, which the present startswith match would miss. If churn is intended instead, say so as I41 did, and exempt generator_sha256 from 'changes no M0-M3 record' explicitly.

findings.what: Some texts the tests compare are defined only in the instrument's code. (1) The tamper 'a contract on M1' requires the gate's G10 detail to contain 'C_t64_m1.json', the file name with its extension (the instrument reports p.name, _i64.py:282). K6 says only that G10 'names each contract, file or law', and the file is a well-formed contract whose id is C_t64_m1, so a G10 that names it by id fails. (2) After a facts change, contracts.json is compared whole with _i64.contracts_doc (test_contracts.py:568). The build must therefore write 'stale: the derived law is not the contract's L_weak over the current facts' (_i64.py:200) verbatim, while K5 shows only 'stale: ...'. (3) The derived law's notes text (_i64.py:163) is compared verbatim at test_contracts.py:315.
findings.why: An honest build that follows the docstring can fail these R3 checks on wording alone.
findings.fix: K6: 'a file G10 cannot attribute to a milestone is named by its file name, <name>.json'. K3 and K5: 'notes and the state texts are exactly those of tests_m3/_i64.derived_law and _i64.states', or list the state strings in K5. Update contract_docstring_sha256.

findings.what: Four differences remain between the instrument and K1/K6, each probed on synthetic trees. (1) l_weak only has to be an object with binders and claim, though K1 says 'an IR 0.3 statement over its facts'. (2) facts accepts an absolute path, or one with '..', whenever the file exists, though K1 says 'a repository path'. With facts '/etc/hostname' problems() reports nothing, and the contract shows as stale, not invalid. (3) Some registry entries are reported by no milestone's G10: an entry that is not an object, or one whose milestone is M0, M1 or any milestone G10 is never run on (an orphan is reported only by its own milestone's G10). REGISTRY.json holding 'C_junk': 5 and an M1 entry with no file gives g10 PASS on T64 and M2, though K6 requires REGISTRY.json to be a holon-contracts-registry/0.1 document. (4) A record in a proved contract's scope that is not JSON is skipped by refuted() and marks(), so G10 passes over it.
findings.why: The fixture exercises none of these, so no outcome changes now. But the instrument is fixed at this commit and defines G10 for I33.
findings.fix: (1) Validate derived_law(c) against law_ir_0_3 in the instrument (tests.reference.mini_schema), or state in K1 that derive (K3) checks it. (2) Require facts and view.facts to be relative, without '..'. (3) In g10, report every registry entry that is not {milestone, kind, sha256} of strings, and every entry for a milestone G10 never runs on. (4) Fail on an unreadable record named by a scope. Update instrument_sha256, and contract_docstring_sha256 if K1 or K6 change.

findings.what: baseline() makes a copy_repo() (about 476 MB of this checkout) and never removes it. When run_t64 raises, nothing is cached, so each later caller makes and leaks another copy. At the prereg, seven tests leave a copy each, about 3.3 GB per red run: test_apply_and_derive_on_a_copy, test_the_least_id_names_the_mark, test_derive_writes_the_l_weak_laws, test_g10_agrees_with_the_instrument_on_t64, test_g10_fails_on_each_tamper, test_p1 and test_p2. A green run leaves one.
findings.why: Repeated red runs during the build can fill /tmp, so that later checks fail on disk errors that have nothing to do with I64. I41's T41 suite removes its copy in tearDownClass.
findings.fix: In baseline(), remove repo.parent and re-raise when run_t64 raises, or cache the exception. Add tearDownModule() to remove _RUNS['base'][0].parent.

One is K5's last step on the typed runners (holon.undo.run, holon.disch.run: 'whichever runner decides the milestone (typed or not)'): T64 runs only through holon.pipeline. The other is apply's three refusals with exit 2: results/M not a directory, a record that is not JSON, a record holding half a mark.
